mostWorthwhile.text: The impact that formed the Moon was most worthwhile: debris gathering into a companion that reflects sunlight made the result both satisfying and understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Illuminating the rocky world was a less compelling detour: it produced light but did not advance the nighttime-light goal.

surprise.text: Air tilting the rocky world surprised me; the later explanation that axial tilt drives seasons was useful, even though the air-to-tilt link remained unclear.

arbitrary.text: Air producing axial tilt lacked a clear physical rationale, despite the useful explanation that followed.

continue.text: Yes. The Moon's impact sequence and the explanation of seasons made me curious to see whether another chapter would offer similarly understandable discoveries.
